## Spread spectrum modulation

- A narrowband signal ($s[n]$) concentrates most of its power in a very small frequency interval.
- Problem: what if another narrowband signal or intereference occupies the same frequency band?
  - Impact: the narrowband signal may be completely masked by the interference, and it cannot be detected or demodulated.


```{python}
from IPython.display import HTML
import numpy as np
import plotly.graph_objects as go
import plotly.io as pio

# Frequency axis (normalized to the carrier frequency)
f = np.linspace(-5, 5, 2001);

# Narrowband signal: Gaussian-shaped PSD concentrated around DC
sigma_n = 0.35;
psd_narrow = np.exp(-(f / sigma_n) ** 2); # Max value is 1 at f=0

# Calculate area of narrowband signal using numerical integration
area_narrow = np.trapz(psd_narrow, f);

# Spread-spectrum signal: Gaussian-shaped over a wider bandwidth
sigma_c = 2.0; # Wider sigma for spread spectrum
psd_spread_raw = np.exp(-(f / sigma_c) ** 2); # Max value is 1 at f=0

# Calculate area of raw spread-spectrum signal
area_spread_raw = np.trapz(psd_spread_raw, f);

# Scale spread-spectrum signal to have the same area as narrowband signal
scale_factor = area_narrow / area_spread_raw;
psd_spread = scale_factor * psd_spread_raw;

# Interfering signal: Gaussian-shaped, designed to almost mask the narrowband signal
sigma_i = 0.1;
peak_amplitude_i = 1.4;
frequency_shift = 0.2; # Shift the interfering signal to the right
psd_interfering = peak_amplitude_i * np.exp(-((f - frequency_shift) / sigma_i) ** 2);

fig = go.Figure();
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=f, y=psd_narrow, mode='lines', name='Narrowband (s)', line=dict(color='royalblue', width=3)));
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=f, y=psd_interfering, mode='lines', name='Interfering Signal', line=dict(color='red', width=3), visible=True));
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=f, y=psd_spread, mode='lines', name='Spread spectrum (c)', line=dict(color='green', width=3), visible=True));

# Define bandwidths (e.g., 2*sigma as a proxy for effective bandwidth)
B_s = 2 * sigma_n;
B_c = 2 * sigma_c;
B_i = 2 * sigma_i;

# Define y-coordinates for the bandwidth arrows and annotations
# Place narrowband arrow slightly above its peak (which is 1)
arrow_y_narrow = 1.05;
# Place interfering signal arrow at a higher level to avoid overlap
arrow_y_interfering = np.max(psd_interfering) + 0.2;
# Place spread spectrum arrow slightly above its peak (which is scale_factor)
arrow_y_spread = np.max(psd_spread) + 0.05;

fig.update_layout(
    title='Spread Spectrum modulation principle',
    xaxis_title='Frequency',
    yaxis_title='Power Spectral Density',
    template='plotly_white',
    legend=dict(orientation='h', yanchor='bottom', y=1.02, xanchor='right', x=1),
    margin=dict(l=50, r=20, t=50, b=50),
    height=420,
    width=820,
    annotations=[
        # Narrowband bandwidth text label
        dict(
            x=0, y=arrow_y_narrow + 0.05,
            text=f'B<sub>s</sub>',
            showarrow=False,
            font=dict(color="royalblue", size=12),
            yanchor="bottom"
        ),
        # Narrowband bandwidth double-sided arrow
        dict(
            x=B_s/2, y=arrow_y_narrow,
            ax=-B_s/2, ay=arrow_y_narrow,
            xref="x", yref="y", axref="x", ayref="y",
            showarrow=True,
            arrowhead=3, arrowsize=1, arrowwidth=2, arrowcolor="royalblue",
            arrowside="start+end"
        ),
        # Interfering signal bandwidth text label
        dict(
            x=frequency_shift, y=arrow_y_interfering + 0.05,
            text=f'B<sub>i</sub>',
            showarrow=False,
            font=dict(color="red", size=12),
            yanchor="bottom",
            visible=True
        ),
        # Interfering signal bandwidth double-sided arrow
        dict(
            x=frequency_shift + B_i/2, y=arrow_y_interfering,
            ax=frequency_shift - B_i/2, ay=arrow_y_interfering,
            xref="x", yref="y", axref="x", ayref="y",
            showarrow=True,
            arrowhead=3, arrowsize=1, arrowwidth=2, arrowcolor="red",
            arrowside="start+end",
            visible=True
        ),
        # Spread spectrum bandwidth text label
        dict(
            x=0, y=arrow_y_spread + 0.05,
            text=f'B<sub>c</sub>',
            showarrow=False,
            font=dict(color="green", size=12),
            yanchor="bottom",
            visible=True
        ),
        # Spread spectrum bandwidth double-sided arrow
        dict(
            x=B_c/2, y=arrow_y_spread,
            ax=-B_c/2, ay=arrow_y_spread,
            xref="x", yref="y", axref="x", ayref="y",
            showarrow=True,
            arrowhead=3, arrowsize=1, arrowwidth=2, arrowcolor="green",
            arrowside="start+end",
            visible=True
        )
    ]
);

# Remove numerical x-ticks and y-ticks for a qualitative plot
fig.update_xaxes(showticklabels=False);
fig.update_yaxes(showticklabels=False, range=[0, 1.5]); # Keep range for consistent visual scale
HTML(pio.to_html(fig, full_html=False, include_plotlyjs='cdn', include_mathjax=False))
```

## Spread spectrum modulation

- By multiplying the information-bearing waveform by a much faster pseudorandom sequence, the transmitted energy is spread over a much wider bandwidth, producing a nearly flat power spectral density across the occupied band.


The signal bandwidth increases dramatically, but the power density in any given narrow slice of spectrum decreases. This is the key reason GNSS signals can coexist on the same frequency band while preserving good ranging performance and resistance to narrowband interference.
